question.text: One mole crystal of a metal halide of the type <math> <mrow> <mtext>MX</mtext></mrow> </math> with molecular weight <math> <mrow> <mtext>119</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>g</mtext></mrow> </math> having face centered cubic structure with unit cell length <math> <mrow> <mtext>6</mtext><mtext>.58</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>Å</mtext></mrow> </math> was recrystallized. The density of the recrystallized crystal was found to be <math><mn>2.44</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The type of defect introduced during the recrystalization may be

options.text: additional <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions at interstitial sites

solution.text:
Calculated density d=Z×moler massNa×volume=2.78 gcm-3
Is greater then actual density 2.44 gcm-3 therefore density decreases and defect is Schottky defect
